composition.serve_who: This sheet (GMMS 108'-124, "Cockpit Hydraulic Control Panels") shows two mirrored cockpit console panels — PORT and STBD — each carrying a bank of pushbuttons labelled FURL/JIB, STAYSAIL(FURL), JIB TACK UP/DOWN, JIB SHEET UP/DOWN, IN, OUT with paired red LED indicators, wired via numbered terminal strips and multi-core cables (MU-X1P/X2P port, MU-X1S/X2S stbd) down into a shared "AFT MYT PLC J/BOX" containing PORT/STBD DI/DO terminal columns feeding a MYT PLC (DI-04/05, DO-01 channels) and a 4-relay bank (Re1-4) whose output lands on a terminal labelled MYT and continues off-sheet "to STBD PEDESTAL J/BOX 3". By function-name match against engineer-confirmed mappings: FURL/JIB -> Bamar GFSI30 jib furler (860-bamar-gfsi30); STAYSAIL(FURL) -> Bamar SIT20 staysail furler (860-bamar-sit20); the unlabelled first FURL row (row1, likely Code-0/general furl) -> Bamar PI20 (860-bamar-pi20). JIB TACK UP/DOWN and JIB SHEET UP/DOWN/IN/OUT are cylinder-actuation commands consistent with Cariboni hydraulic cylinders (840-cariboni-hydraulic-cylinders), per the established fact already recording 'JIB TACK UP/DOWN' and 'JIB SHEET UP' cockpit_control entries against that node. The AFT MYT PLC J/BOX, its DI/DO terminal structure, +24V PLC rail, and the Re1-4 relay bank are shared PLC I/O infrastructure and attach to the AFT PLC I/O Rack node (570-plc-rack-aft), not to any single sail function. The actual hydraulic valve/cylinder wiring downstream of these pushbutton commands is not drawn on this sheet — only the button-to-PLC-input wiring is shown; the valve/manifold end is cross-referenced to the sailing manifold hydraulic schematics.

equipment_groups.placement_reasoning: Engineer-confirmed mapping: 'FURL JIB' -> 860-bamar-gfsi30; 'JIB' button (terminal 2) -> 860-bamar-gfsi30 per established fact from this same sheet (GMMS 108'-124).

functions.label: FURL / JIB pushbutton command (PORT and STBD consoles)
functions.what_it_does: Momentary pushbutton on both port and stbd cockpit consoles commands furling/unfurling of the jib via the MYT PLC; each button is wired to its console terminal strip terminal 2, then via multi-core cable (MU-X1P/X2P port, MU-X1S/X2S stbd) to the AFT MYT PLC J/BOX PLC input columns.
functions.sheet_region: PORT panel top-left (bbox 0.0-0.30,0.19-0.42) and STBD panel top-right (bbox 0.70-1.0,0.19-0.42); AFT MYT PLC J/BOX (0.33-0.66,0.56-0.93)

flow_scenarios.path: button open -> no signal on terminal 2 -> PLC input not asserted -> LED off

operator presses JIB pushbutton (port or stbd console) -> closes contact to terminal 2 -> signal travels via multi-core cable MU-X1P/X2P (port) or MU-X1S/X2S (stbd) -> AFT MYT PLC J/BOX DI terminal column -> MYT PLC reads command and drives furler; paired red LED illuminates to confirm button press/engagement

functions.dry_data: 24V DC pushbutton input to WAGO-type PLC DI, mirrored port/stbd consoles

operator presses STAYSAIL pushbutton -> closes contact to terminal 3 -> via MU-X1P/X2P or MU-X1S/X2S -> AFT MYT PLC J/BOX DI column -> MYT PLC drives staysail furler; LED confirms

functions.label: JIB TACK UP / DOWN pushbutton commands (PORT and STBD consoles)
functions.what_it_does: Two momentary pushbuttons move the jib tack hydraulic cylinder up or down; wired to terminals 4 (UP) and 5 (DOWN) on both port and stbd consoles, through the multi-core cable to the PLC J/Box.
functions.sheet_region: PORT panel rows 4-5 (0.0-0.30,0.19-0.42), STBD panel rows 4-5 (0.70-1.0,0.19-0.42), AFT MYT PLC J/BOX

flow_scenarios.path: both buttons open -> no signal on terminal 4 or 5 -> cylinder holds position -> LEDs off

operator presses JIB TACK UP -> closes contact terminal 4 -> via multi-core cable (MU-X1P/X2P or MU-X1S/X2S) -> AFT MYT PLC J/BOX DI column -> MYT PLC actuates cylinder extend/retract (up direction); LED confirms
operator presses JIB TACK DOWN -> closes contact terminal 5 -> via multi-core cable -> AFT MYT PLC J/BOX DI column -> MYT PLC actuates cylinder opposite direction; LED confirms

functions.dry_data: 24V DC pushbutton pair to PLC DI, mirrored port/stbd

functions.label: JIB SHEET UP / DOWN, IN / OUT pushbutton commands (PORT and STBD consoles)
functions.what_it_does: Four momentary pushbuttons (JIB SHEET UP, DOWN, IN, OUT) command the jib sheet hydraulic cylinder/winch; wired to terminals 6 (UP), 7 (DOWN), 8 (IN), 9 (OUT) on both consoles.
functions.sheet_region: PORT panel rows 6-9 (0.0-0.30,0.19-0.42), STBD panel rows 6-9 (0.70-1.0,0.19-0.42), AFT MYT PLC J/BOX

flow_scenarios.path: all buttons open -> no signal on terminals 6-9 -> LEDs off
press JIB SHEET UP -> terminal 6 -> multi-core cable -> AFT MYT PLC J/BOX -> MYT PLC actuates sheet cylinder; LED confirms
press JIB SHEET DOWN -> terminal 7 -> multi-core cable -> AFT MYT PLC J/BOX -> MYT PLC actuates sheet cylinder opposite; LED confirms
press IN -> terminal 8 -> multi-core cable -> AFT MYT PLC J/BOX -> MYT PLC drives sheet in; LED confirms
press OUT -> terminal 9 -> multi-core cable -> AFT MYT PLC J/BOX -> MYT PLC drives sheet out; LED confirms

equipment_groups.equipment_name: MYT Aft-area PLC / relay control (AFT MYT PLC J/BOX)
equipment_groups.placement_reasoning: The J/Box is a titled PLC I/O infrastructure enclosure (dashed boundary) holding PORT/STBD DI/DO terminal columns, +24V PLC rail, and a 4-relay bank (Re1-4) — shared infrastructure serving all cockpit console commands, matching the AFT PLC I/O Rack node rather than any single sail function.

functions.label: PLC DI/DO processing and Re1-4 relay bank
functions.what_it_does: Receives all PORT/STBD console pushbutton signals on DI channels (DI-04 CH07 port, DI-05 CH04 stbd, plus others), applies +24V PLC supply to inputs, and drives 4 output relays (Re1-Re4) whose contacts report status back on DI-05 CH12 and whose combined output lands on a terminal labelled 'MYT', continuing off-sheet to STBD PEDESTAL J/BOX 3.
functions.sheet_region: AFT MYT PLC J/BOX dashed enclosure (bbox 0.32-0.68,0.56-0.93); relay bank (0.46-0.58,0.72-0.83)

flow_scenarios.path: no console button pressed -> DI channels not asserted -> relays Re1-4 de-energised -> DI-05 CH12 status lines reflect off state

PLC logic asserts DO-01 CH13 (port) or CH16 (stbd) -> +24V PLC feed at terminal 10 -> energises relay coil (Re1/Re2/Re3/Re4, contact type not confirmed on this sheet) -> relay contact closes/opens -> status reported to DI-05 CH12 -> combined signal reaches terminal strip pin 1 labelled MYT -> continues off-sheet via multi-core cable to STBD PEDESTAL J/BOX 3 (cross-reference, not detailed here)

functions.dry_data: WAGO-style PLC I/O module, +24V DC supply, DI-04 CH07/DI-05 CH04 inputs, DO-01 CH13/CH16 outputs, DI-05 CH12 relay status feedback

facts: Each console (port and stbd) has its own back-lighting +/- pair wired to lower terminal strip terminals 5 (+) and 6 (-)
No node exists specifically for console panel back-lighting as a distinct equipment; treated as console infrastructure, not attached to a sailing-function node
Not a separate lighting circuit fed from a lighting panel node (690-lts-*) since no such link is drawn on this sheet — this is local panel illumination wired through the console's own terminal strip

infrastructure.system_name: Console LED indicator bank supply (PORT and STBD)
facts: Each console has a bank of red LED indicators (one per pushbutton function, 9 total) fed from a shared + rail (terminal 10/marked +) and returning on a common bus to terminals 11/12

The LED bank's positive feed side traces to console terminal strip terminal 10 (marked +); the negative/return side is a common bus across all 9 LEDs, per the drawn wiring, not an individually traced return for each LED
This shared LED supply rail is console infrastructure (not a separate system) and does not attach to a specific equipment node — it is recorded here as infrastructure of the two mirrored consoles

infrastructure.system_name: Multi-core cable interconnect (MU-X1P/X2P port, MU-X1S/X2S stbd)
facts: Port console connects to AFT MYT PLC J/BOX via two multi-core cable designators MU-X1P and MU-X2P
Stbd console connects to AFT MYT PLC J/BOX via two multi-core cable designators MU-X1S and MU-X2S

These are cable/connector infrastructure carrying all console signals (pushbutton commands + LED returns + back-lighting) between the console terminal strips and the PLC J/Box; they are not equipment in themselves
